findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — [P2 confidence 75] `.small-action { @include flexbox();` — Converting `.small-action-desc` into an auto-sized flex item without `flex-grow` collapses the description to its content width, so its right-floated action button no longer reaches the row edge for short action text.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:35 — [P2 confidence 75] `.panel { position: relative; margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }` — Browsers that select the advertised 2009 `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` fallback treat the auto margin as zero, so removing `float: right` leaves the header panel adjacent to the preceding item instead of right-aligned.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:125 — [P3 confidence 100] `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val;` — Although the current 2/3 call sites preserve their relative order, this shared mixin maps modern zero-based `order` directly onto one-based `box-ordinal-group`, so the next `order(1)` caller renders after default siblings in modern flexbox but tied with them in legacy WebKit/Gecko and forces every caller to understand two ordering models.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

This is a plausible layout regression from the flexbox conversion.
